title: Event-level privacy controls and deletion pipeline for console telemetry
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement a robust, auditable pipeline to scrub, retain, and delete PII from console usage events. This work spans ingestion-side scrub rules, an immutable audit trail for deletion requests, background deletion jobs for raw events and downstream aggregates, and updates to retention configuration in the Console backend services and data pipelines.

Goals:
- Ensure console telemetry cannot be used to identify customers or users beyond the minimum required for product analytics.
- Provide per-customer deletion workflows that are auditable and compliant with common privacy laws (e.g., GDPR/CCPA).
- Maintain operational observability: track deletion progress, failures, and rehydrate aggregates when necessary.

Scope of work:
- Ingest-time PII scrubbing: add field-level scrubbing rules to the telemetry gateway (console-ingest) to remove or hash direct identifiers (emails, API keys, tokens) and reduce free-text capture where possible. Scrubbing configuration is policymapped by event type.
- Deterministic vs. irreversible transformations: use HMAC-sha256 with customer-specific salt for fingerprinting where deduplication is needed; irreversible hashing for identifiers that must not be recoverable. Document trade-offs in decisions below.
- Retention tiers: raw event store retention default 30 days; inferred session-level traces 90 days; rollup metrics (non-identifiable aggregates) 2 years. Provide per-org overrides with approval.
- Deletion workflow: expose an authenticated deletion API for customer requests, create a DeletionJob record (soft-delete marker), run backfill jobs to delete from raw stores (Kafka topic retention + object store), delete from analytical tables (BigQuery/warehouse) and downstream caches, and trigger aggregate recomputations. Record deletion audit entries with job id, scope, and outcome.
- Downstream considerations: coordinate with data-team-owned pipelines (etl-analytics) to ensure logical deletion in aggregated datasets; introduce tombstone markers where immediate physical deletion is impractical.
- Observability & monitoring: add console metrics for deletion job queue depth, per-job error counts, time-to-completion, and a customer-visible deletion status page.
- Compliance docs & runbooks: produce a runbook for escalations, an internal audit doc, and Confluence policy describing retention defaults and exception process.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing full GDPR Right-to-Access flows (handled by a separate ticket).
- Not modifying third-party SaaS that already receives telemetry (we will document and produce mitigation steps).
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline applies configured PII-scrub rules and logs scrub actions to secure audit stream
Deletion API accepts authorized requests and creates a DeletionJob with immutable audit entries
Background deletion worker deletes raw events from object store and marks them as removed in the warehouse within SLA
Aggregates that include deleted records are recomputed or flagged with tombstones within 48 hours
Monitoring dashboards show deletion job progress and alert on failures >5% for a 24h window
Confluence policy and runbook created and reviewed by Legal and Security
tasks: Design scrubbing rules and a canonical event schema (ENG/telemetry-schema RFC)
Add HMAC-salt management in secrets service and integrate with telemetry gateway
Build DeletionJob service and background worker to reconcile object storage and warehouse
Add tombstone markers and aggregate recompute pipeline (etl-analytics coordination)
Instrument metrics and dashboards, add alerts, and customer-visible deletion status endpoint
Security review and Legal sign-off; update compliance docs
decisions: Use HMAC-SHA256 with per-organization salt for deterministic fingerprints (reason: enable event dedup while minimizing re-identification risk). Salt rotation will be supported but will break deterministic fingerprints for rotated events.
Apply irreversible hashing (sha256 with no salt) for email addresses when customers opt-in for deletion-only retention (reason: defense-in-depth if salts leak).
Default raw event retention set to 30 days to limit exposure; allow seat-based org overrides after Security & Legal approval.

Physical deletion schedule: raw object store files will be removed immediately by worker; warehouse deletion will be handled via batch delete with tombstones for incremental pipelines to prevent query failures.
